items.title: Add new license MRSL-1.0
items.body:
Reference: https://github.com/aboutcode-org/scancode-toolkit/issues/5324

Fixes #5324

Adds the MitsuoLabs Reciprocity and Stewardship License 1.0 (MRSL-1.0).

### Changes
- New license `mrsl-1.0` (SPDX: LicenseRef-scancode-mrsl-1.0), category: Copyleft

### Verification
- `scancode-reindex-licenses` completes without errors
- Scanning the license text detects `mrsl-1.0` (score: 100.0, coverage: 100.0)
- `SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-scancode-mrsl-1.0` is detected
- License-data tests pass locally

### For reviewers
- Category is a judgment call: Part I is strong + network copyleft (like AGPL-3.0); Part II adds an optional Steward-only covenant (Hippocratic-style "Free Restricted" is the alternative).
- The text has placeholders ([[YEAR]] etc.), and its "canonical source" line points to a different URL than the issue and the text's footer. I used the issue's URL as `homepage_url`.
- The text says it is itself licensed under MRSL-1.0. Flagging in case that matters for including it as data.
- Note: I did not add separate `.RULE` files as the full text indexing yielded 100% coverage automatically, but let me know if you need specific short-phrase rules added!

### Tasks

* [x] Reviewed [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
* [x] PR is descriptively titled 📑 and links the original issue above 🔗
* [ ] Tests pass -- look for a green checkbox ✔️ a few minutes after opening your PR
  Run [tests](https://scancode-toolkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contribute/contrib_dev.html#running-tests) locally to check for errors. 
* [x] Commits are in uniquely-named feature branch and has no merge conflicts 📁
* [ ] Updated documentation pages (if applicable)
* [ ] Updated CHANGELOG.rst (if applicable)

items.body:
**License Name**
MitsuoLabs Reciprocity and Stewardship License 1.0 (MRSL-1.0)

License Homepage URL https://mitsuolabs.github.io/LegalFramework/mrsl-1.0.txt

**Reference URLs**

Official GitHub Repository: https://github.com/MitsuoLabs/LegalFramework

Launch Manifesto & Philosophical Foundation: https://mitsuolabs.com/mitsuolabs-legal-framework-the-grand-return

**License Notes**
The MitsuoLabs Reciprocity and Stewardship License Version 1.0 (MRSL-1.0) is a pioneering, future-proof legal and ethical constitutional framework engineered specifically for the 2050s and beyond. It moves beyond 1990s-era open-source paradigms by establishing a robust dual-regime architecture designed to govern the digital commons while protecting human dignity, software integrity, and epistemic sovereignty against corporate capture and cognitive warfare.

1. Dual-Regime Architectural Breakdown

Part I (The Core Public License): Functions as the universal FOSS baseline. It irrevocably grants the four fundamental software freedoms (Use, Study, Modify, Distribute) to the entire public without field-of-use restrictions. It incorporates strong copyleft reciprocity for "Integrated Works" (GPL-like) while providing clean off-ramps for "System Works" (LGPL-like library linking). Furthermore, it closes the modern "SaaS Loophole" via stringent Network Reciprocity (requiring source availability for cloud and API services) and mandates a 90-day Right of Repair for unpatched critical vulnerabilities ($\text{CVSS} \ge 9.0$). It also establishes the Alexandria Clause, requiring good-faith digital preservation in non-profit archives.

Part II (The Stewardship Rider): An optional, bilateral contractual covenant. Developers and contributors ("Stewards") who voluntarily opt in via a verifiable STEWARD.md declaration receive advanced legal and governance rights—including irrevocable patent indemnification, mutual defense pacts, and formalized project governance priority. In exchange, Stewards bind themselves to the strict Ethical Use Covenant, pledging that their specific contributions will not be used for mass surveillance, weaponized synthetic consciousness, unwatermarked deepfakes, or retrospective quantum decryption (HNDL).

2. Technological Scope & Future-Proofing

MRSL-1.0 is engineered explicitly for emerging computational paradigms that legacy licenses entirely ignore:

Artificial Intelligence & Synthetic Agents: Regulates AI-assisted contributions, model training provenance, and requires permanent watermarking for deceptive synthetic media.

Quantum Computing Systems: Anticipates the post-quantum panopticon by explicitly banning "Retrospective Cryptographic Violation" (using quantum systems to retroactively decrypt historical data).

Human-Machine Interface Devices (HMIDs): Protects neural data sovereignty and prohibits non-consensual neural stimulation or biometric exploitation.

3. Compliance and Ecosystem Integration

The framework is designed for practical interoperability, featuring a built-in compatibility bridge for the GPL family and clear integration guidelines with permissive and ethical-source licenses, ensuring that sovereign projects can adopt the constitution without breaking upstream ecosystems.

labels.name: new-license
labels.description: A new scancode license can be added for this

items.body:
### License Name

Qwen Research License Agreement (Release Date: September 19, 2024)

### License Homepage URL

https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B/blob/main/LICENSE

### Reference URLs

- Raw text: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B/raw/main/LICENSE
- Same text shipped in: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct/blob/main/LICENSE and https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B/blob/main/LICENSE
- Hugging Face's license identifier table (this license has no Hub id; repos use `license: other` + `license_name: qwen-research`): https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/repositories-licenses

### License Notes

- Distinct from the "Qwen License Agreement" already keyed as `qwen-2024`
  (Qwen2.5-72B etc.) and from `tongyi-qianwen-2023`: this one is the
  research/non-commercial agreement used by the 3B-class Qwen2.5 models.
  No `qwen*research*` key exists in LicenseDB (index.json, 2026-08-17). By
  analogy, `qwen-research-2024` would fit; your call.
- Single version as far as checked: the LICENSE files in the three repos above
  are byte-identical (7,388 bytes, 1,156 words, SHA-256
  `ef52482bb785733093dc9a2e8edd8e764c77d12d8e9d8f10a80c9b547d32d0f9`, fetched
  2026-08-17).
- Usage: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B` alone lists 436 adapters, 512 finetunes, 17 merges
  and 53 quantizations in its model tree (2026-08-17); on the Hub the license
  appears as `license: other` with `license_name: qwen-research`, so it is not
  filterable by facet.
- Small metadata note while checking: `qwen-2024` and `tongyi-qianwen-2023`
  currently list `owner: HuggingFace`; the licensor in both texts is Alibaba
  Cloud. Happy to open a separate issue if useful.

items.title: Add new license bsd-3-clause-cryptogams for the CRYPTOGAMS license
items.body:
Fixes #5253

Adds `bsd-3-clause-cryptogams` for the CRYPTOGAMS license (the BSD-3-Clause variant used by Andy Polyakov's CRYPTOGAMS cryptographic assembly modules, with an alternative clause allowing distribution under the GPL instead), using the name suggested in the issue. Text from the LICENSE file of https://github.com/dot-asm/cryptogams; SPDX has no identifier for it (checked the current license list), so `spdx_license_key: LicenseRef-scancode-bsd-3-clause-cryptogams`.

`category: Permissive`, with the GPL-alternative clause recorded in `notes`.

Detection before this change: the text matched `bsd-new OR gpl-1.0-plus`, which approximates the semantics but loses the CRYPTOGAMS identity that tools like ORT need to track these files precisely. It now detects as `bsd-3-clause-cryptogams` with score 100.

Validation (same for all six license additions from this batch):

- `scancode-reindex-licenses` runs clean
- self-detection and ignorables validation tests pass (`--test-suite=validate tests/licensedcode/test_detection_validate.py`), with ignorables generated by the test regen tooling rather than by hand
- `pytest tests/licensedcode/test_license_models.py` passes locally

items.title: Add new license llama-3-license-2024 for Meta Llama 3
items.body:
Fixes #5269

Adds a new license `llama-3-license-2024` for the Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement (Meta Llama 3 Version Release Date: April 18, 2024), which was not yet in LicenseDB (the 3.1/3.2/3.3 agreements are separately titled and already keyed).

Choices made, following the existing `llama-2-license-2023`, `llama-3.1-license-2024` and `llama-3.2-license-2024` entries:

- key `llama-3-license-2024` by analogy with the sibling keys, as suggested in the issue
- `category: Proprietary Free`, `owner: Facebook`, `spdx_license_key: LicenseRef-scancode-llama-3-license-2024`
- the text is the agreement as published at https://github.com/meta-llama/llama3/blob/main/LICENSE (fetched from the raw URL in the issue), without the appended "Meta Llama 3 Acceptable Use Policy", consistent with the sibling entries which all end at section 7 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction)

Validation:

- `scancode-reindex-licenses` runs clean
- scanning the full upstream LICENSE file (agreement + appended AUP) now detects the agreement portion as `llama-3-license-2024` with score 100 (lines 1-41). The appended AUP portion still partially matches `llama-4-license-2025` (score ~66); if you want a dedicated rule or key for the Llama 3 AUP text I am happy to add it here or in a follow-up.

items.title: Add new license segv-1.1 for the SEGV License 1.1
items.body:
Fixes #5247

Adds `segv-1.1` for the SEGV License Version 1.1 (July 2026), text from the cloudcash LICENSE file referenced in the issue, homepage set to https://xn--gckvb8fzb.com/segv/.

As the issue notes, its Appendix B states it is adapted from the Hippocratic License 3.0 with modified and additional terms; this is recorded in the `notes` field, and `category: Free Restricted` mirrors the existing `hippocratic-3.0` entry. `owner: Unspecified` since the license text itself names no steward -- happy to change if you prefer attributing it to its author.

Detection before this change: the text partially matched `hippocratic-1.2` plus unknown license references. It now detects as `segv-1.1` with score 100.

Validation (same for all six license additions from this batch):

- `scancode-reindex-licenses` runs clean
- self-detection and ignorables validation tests pass (`--test-suite=validate tests/licensedcode/test_detection_validate.py`), with ignorables generated by the test regen tooling rather than by hand
- `pytest tests/licensedcode/test_license_models.py` passes locally

items.title: Add new license qwen-research-2024 for the Qwen Research License Agreement
items.body:
Fixes #5270

Adds `qwen-research-2024` for the Qwen Research License Agreement (Release Date: September 19, 2024), the research/non-commercial agreement used by the 3B-class Qwen2.5 models. The text was fetched from the raw URL in the issue and its SHA-256 matches the one documented there (`ef52482b…d32d0f9`).

Choices, following the existing `qwen-2024` entry: key `qwen-research-2024` as suggested in the issue, `category: Proprietary Free` and `owner: HuggingFace` mirroring `qwen-2024` (happy to change either if you prefer e.g. Free Restricted given the non-commercial research scope). A `notes` field records that this is distinct from `qwen-2024` and `tongyi-qianwen-2023`.

Detection before this change: the text matched `qwen-2024 AND proprietary-license`, i.e. it was misattributed to the wrong Qwen agreement. It now detects as `qwen-research-2024` with score 100.
